title: Receipts/DuplicateKeyMemberSilentlyDroppedTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 2 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1, logic-edge-2

refutes.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards around `intMembers.Add` and `stringMembers.Add` keep the first member and silently drop any later member with the same key. This applies to every type, not only `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types. For a plain `[MessagePackObject]` class with two `[Key(0)]` properties, base threw inside `TypeCollector` (AD0001 / CS8785, so the error was visible). Head reports nothing and emits a formatter that never serializes the second property. That breaks the acceptance criterion that behaviour without `SuppressSourceGeneration` does not change. It also silently loses data where the dynamic resolver rejects the duplicate key. The same applies to string keys.

The same first-wins duplicate-key guard is in the `SuppressSourceGeneration`/`contractAttr` branch at line 1175, for both int and string keys. The analyzer now says nothing about colliding keys, which the dynamic resolver rejects at run time. A suppressed type with duplicate keys therefore passes the build cleanly and fails only at run time.
